details: Bitcoin (BTC) has fallen below $82,000, dropping approximately 4% as the broader cryptocurrency market experiences a sell-off. This downturn is attributed to rising oil prices, escalating geopolitical tensions involving the US and Iran, and growing investor caution regarding artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending. Altcoins, including Ethereum, XRP, and Solana, also saw declines of over 4%. Technology stocks, particularly chip companies like Nvidia and Meta, also plunged, reflecting concerns about AI spending.
title: Bitcoin Dips Amid Macroeconomic Headwinds and AI Spending Concerns

details: Japan's core inflation surpassed the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) 2% target in September, the first time in nine months. This strengthens the case for a potential December rate hike, with the US Federal Reserve also expected to raise rates around the same time. Rising Japanese rates could lead investors to unwind yen carry trades, potentially pressuring cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin has already declined by 5.6% over the past month and 3.16% in the last 24 hours.
title: Japan's Inflation Exceeds Target, Rate Hike Speculation Impacts Bitcoin

details: The Central Bank of Ireland has fined Coinbase's Irish unit €3.25 million ($3.65 million) for failing to meet safeguarding and outsourcing obligations between 2020 and 2025. While Coinbase stated that no customers suffered financial loss, the fine highlights regulatory scrutiny on crypto platforms regarding consumer protection and financial stability.
title: Irish Central Bank Fines Coinbase for Safeguarding Breaches

details: US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded a two-week streak of net withdrawals, totaling $146.19 million through Thursday, with $635 million in net outflows on October 23 alone. This suggests weakening institutional demand for Bitcoin and contributes to the current selling pressure. Despite some recent inflows for Ether and Solana ETFs, the overall trend for Bitcoin ETFs indicates cautious sentiment.
title: Bitcoin Spot ETF Outflows Continue, Signaling Weakening Demand
